newsitem.title: GERMANY: Pfleiderer outlines plans to offer shares.
newsitem.headline: Pfleiderer outlines plans to offer shares.

text.p: German building materials supplier Pfleiderer Unternehmensverwaltung GmbH is making "concrete plans" to offer shares within the next few years, chief executive Hans-Peter Mall said on Wednesday.

The family-owned concern, which had revenues of 1.8 billion marks ($1.2 billion) in the 1995-96 business year, is considering forming a public holding company overseeing its subsidiaries, but has not ruled out other options, Mall said.
It could also choose to issue shares in just one of its units, as it has already done with its delivery business, Pfleiderer Bau- und Verkehrsysteme AG, Mall said.
Whatever the case, the family would keep a clear majority of shares, he said. Mall outlined no set timetable, but said the offering should occur well within five years.
For the business year ended May 31, Pfleiderer failed to reach its sales target of two billion marks, although pre-tax profit rose 13 percent to 78 million marks.

Mall said sales so far this year are running above expectations and should reach the two billion mark level in 1996-97. He credited the rise to a new 200 million mark particle board plant in Neumarkt and new business in Asia, the United States and Eastern Europe.
-- Neal Boudette, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-2609750 ($ = 1.525 German Marks)
